A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniDocBench and contain readable main texts, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Renumbered and relocated appendix content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original end-to-end and component-level document-parsing evaluations, including results across document types and attributes in Tables 2–9 and S1–S2.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations, revises reported results, and adds evaluations of two layout-detection methods.

M1.justification: The extraction, Adjacency Search Match, ignore-handling, and scoring procedures remain substantively unchanged. New Appendix V explains the existing ignore policy without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use 981 pages covering the same nine document types, languages, and attribute categories. Appendix Tables S3–S6 retain the same dataset inventories; revised main-text annotation counts do not establish changed data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds SwinDocSegmenter and GraphKD to the four retained layout-detection comparators. The other comparator sets remain unchanged. Qwen2-VL-72B and InternVL2-Llama3-76B were already identified in v1's model-settings appendix.

E3.justification: Appendix IV changes Marker's specified release from 0.2.17 to 1.2.3. Table 4 adds a comparison group with no special visual issue. Newly disclosed token limits do not establish changes from previously reported limits, since v1 supplied none.

E4.justification: New Figures S3–S4 compare header retention and caption ordering across model outputs to illustrate ignore-handling decisions. Table 4 extends degradation analysis with a no-special-issue group. The extensive existing appendix examples remain unchanged after renumbering.

E5.justification: Tables 4–5 replace summary means and variances across attribute-category scores with mean/variance pairs within each attribute group. This changes descriptive statistical reporting; neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many scores change in Tables 2–5, 7, and S1–S2. In Table 2, Qwen2-VL's Chinese overall edit distance changes from 0.408 to 0.327, replacing Mathpix as the best reported Chinese result. Table 6 adds results and changes DocLayout-YOLO's average from 48.71 to 47.38. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised. The matching and metric descriptions retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract's advertised attribute count changes from 14 to 15, with the contributions specifying six page-level and nine bounding-box-level attributes. The central contribution remains a nine-document-type benchmark supporting end-to-end, task-specific, and attribute-based evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 attributes VLM failures on dense documents to input-resolution and token-length limits and motivates layout-aware processing. Appendix I newly connects MinerU's mixed-language weakness to PaddleOCR. Existing interpretations concerning training diversity, handwriting, and complex layouts are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix IV newly discloses selection of token limits and values of 32000 for Qwen2-VL-72B and 4096 for InternVL2-Llama3-76B. Table 6 adds backbones and parameter counts, and Marker's release information is updated. The benchmark's code and dataset access location remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the prominent READoc discussion, its Table 1 row, and its reference. Related work is substantively reframed around component-level versus full-page evaluation, with new OCRBench discussion and additional method references. This changes the benchmark's positioning beyond bibliographic or stylistic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the results discussion are rewritten. Benchmark subsections are reorganized, terminology shifts toward task-specific evaluation, Appendix III gains a synthesized discussion, and Appendix V is added.

P2.justification: v2 adds a radar summary in Figure 1 and two appendix illustrations, restructures Tables 1 and 4–6, and consolidates the dataset-summary figures onto one page. Most existing diagrams and appendix examples retain their visual content, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility and interpretability through token-budget disclosures, model-size details, additional layout comparisons, and clearer failure analysis. Main-text annotation counts also better match the existing appendix. These gains are limited by the removed READoc context, unexplained score revisions, and Figure 1's Marker-0.2.17 label conflicting with the stated 1.2.3 evaluation.
